title_original: Producer of AI-rendered ‘Gods Don’t Give Gifts’ responds after Academy animation ruling
excerpt_original: AGC International launched sales at AFM.

blocks.text: The producer of AI-rendered sci-fi animation Gods Don’t Give Gifts , directed by YouTuber Gossip Goblin aka Zack London, has responded after the Academy deemed the film ineligible for its animated feature category.

Gods Don’t Give Gifts was not among the Academy’s list of 38 eligible animated features this week. The Academy’s definition of an animated film under the 99th Awards rules state that “characters or objects are given the illusion of life by having movement created for them, by any human means”.
Edward Saatchi of Fable Studios and London have planned a January 22, 2027, US release with an awards-qualifying run starting on December 4.

“It’s up to the Academy where AI fits – that’s a debate that will last way beyond Gods Don’t Give Gifts – but we respect their decisions and we’re excited for people to be able to watch the film and be moved emotionally in the cinema,” Saatchi said. “An audience coming together in the cinema, being moved by a film made by skilled artists – that’s the most important thing.”

Saatchi added, “We’ve submitted for the Oscar’s General Entry as well as for Animation. General Entry includes VFX so it will be up to the Academy both this year and beyond to decide if AI movies fit in animation, in VFX, as their own category – it’s going to be a great debate in the years to come.”
Gods Don’t Give Gifts takes place in the so-called Second Cycle of Humanity where transhumanism has taken root and the physical limits around humanity have begun to disappear.

AGC International screened the feature for AFM buyers and fans of the director’s work last month. London said, “AI was a tool to help us tell our story at scale, while still being able to maintain our core artistic vision without having to compromise or answer to other parties.”
